teaser.en: Swahili speakers everywhere know *mchicha*, but this tall amaranth goes by the same name in Digo gardens.

summary.en: *Mchicha* is a tall amaranth grown in gardens and farms. Its leaves are cooked as greens, one of the most common vegetables of the coast.

about.en: *Mchicha* is a tall, leafy herb with oval leaves on long stalks and dense spikes of tiny green or reddish flowers at the tips. It grows fast and can be harvested by picking leaves again and again.

where.en: It is grown in gardens and on farms across the south coast.

uses.en: The leaves are cooked as greens.

names.en: The Digo name is *mchicha*, the same as in Swahili. In English it is amaranth or pigweed. Digo also uses *mtsunga* for vegetables, especially amaranths.

reason.en: Another leafy green of the garden
Another leaf vegetable eaten with ugali

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: An ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD diss., Univ. Bayreuth (Appendix III & Table G.2) https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
